title: My World
subtitle: All About Me

project.title: My World Profile
project.description: Create a personal profile and introduce the people who are important to you. The project grows lesson by lesson.
project.deliverable: A personal My World profile with an identity card and a family tree, presented in simple English.
successCriteria: I can introduce myself and give basic personal information.
I can talk about family members and relationships.
I can use plural nouns and possessive adjectives.
I can use this, that, these and those to identify people and things.
I can present my family tree in simple English.

objectives: Introduce yourself and ask for basic personal information.
Name family members and describe family relationships.
Use regular and irregular plural nouns.
Use possessive adjectives and this, that, these and those.
Create and present a personal profile and family tree.

vocabulary.example: My family is important to me.
My school is near my home.

grammar.title: Verb be
grammar.rule: I am · You are · He/She/It is · We/They are

grammar.title: Have got
grammar.rule: I/You/We/They have got · He/She has got

grammar.title: Possessive adjectives
grammar.rule: my · your · his · her · our · their

grammar.title: There is / There are
grammar.rule: There is + one thing · There are + two or more things
examples: There is a desk in my room.
There are two parks near my home.

grammar.title: Present Simple: likes and routines
grammar.rule: I like / I play / I go · He likes / He plays / He goes

screens.title: Welcome to My World
screens.body: Every person has a world: people, places, interests and everyday moments. Let’s discover yours — and learn how to talk about it in English.
screens.prompt: Your final mission is to create a My World Profile. Each activity will help you build one part of it.

screens.title: Look. Think. Connect.
screens.body: Look at the three photographs. What connects them? Choose the ideas that come to your mind, then make a guess about our topic.
screens.question: What can connect people, places and interests?
screens.feedback: Think about the people around you, the places you know and the things you enjoy. They are all part of your world.

screens.title: Your mission
screens.body: Create a personal profile in English. Imagine you are introducing yourself to a new international friend.
steps: Describe people who are important to you.
Talk about your home and hometown.
Share your interests and daily routine.

screens.title: Words for your world
screens.body: Explore the key words. Read each example aloud and think of a true sentence about your own life.

screens.title: Vocabulary check
screens.body: Choose the best word to complete each sentence.

questions.q: My ___ is Anna. Nice to meet you.
questions.why: We use name to say what a person is called.
Live means to have your home in a place.
Favourite means the one you like most.

screens.title: Grammar Lab 1 · Verb be
screens.body: Use be to give basic information and describe people and places.

screens.title: Build a sentence
screens.body: Choose the correct form of be.

questions.why: Use is with he, she and it.

screens.title: Reading · Meet Mia
screens.body: Read Mia’s profile. Notice how she introduces herself and describes her world.
screens.text: Hi! My name is Mia and I’m 13. I live in a small town near the sea. I’ve got one brother and a friendly dog called Max. My best friend is Lily. We are in the same class. I like drawing and listening to music. At weekends, I usually ride my bike with Lily. There is a lovely park near my house.

options: In a small town near the sea

questions.q: What does Mia do at weekends?

screens.title: Grammar Lab 2 · Have got
screens.body: Use have got to talk about family members, pets and possessions.

screens.title: My people
screens.body: Complete the sentences with have got, has got, my or her.

items.hint: Use a possessive adjective before a noun.

screens.title: Grammar Lab 3 · There is / There are
screens.body: Describe a room, a home or a place in your town.

screens.title: Describe a place
screens.body: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.why: Use There is with one thing.
Use There are with plural nouns.

screens.title: Listening · A new friend
screens.body: Listen to the short introduction. Then answer the questions. If audio is unavailable, use the transcript toggle.
screens.audioText: Hello! I'm Ben. I'm twelve years old and I live in Bristol. I've got a big family: two sisters and one brother. I love skateboarding and I play basketball after school. My favourite place is the park near my home.

questions.q: How many sisters has Ben got?
What does Ben do after school?

screens.title: Project Workshop · Build your profile
screens.body: Use the prompts to create the first version of your My World Profile. You can edit it before the final presentation.

fields.label: My name and age
fields.placeholder: My name is ... I am ... years old.

fields.label: People important to me
fields.placeholder: I have got ... My best friend is ...

screens.title: Challenge · Your new classmate
screens.body: A new student joins your class. They do not know anyone yet. Help them feel welcome.
screens.scenario: You have one minute to introduce yourself and ask two friendly questions.
prompts: Have you got any brothers or sisters?

screens.title: Present your world
screens.body: Bring your profile together. Read it aloud or record a 60–90 second presentation. Use the checklist before you finish.
checklist: I described at least one person.

screens.title: Look back · What can you do now?
screens.body: Think about your progress. Honest reflection helps you choose the next step.
questions: I can introduce myself in English.
I can describe people and places.
I can talk about my interests and routine.
I can present my My World Profile.

screens.title: Look closer: who is part of your world?
screens.body: Look at the three photographs. What connects the people? Think about the different generations and relationships in a family.

images.alt: A family spending time together outdoors
images.caption: A family together

screens.question: What is today's topic?
screens.prompt: Who is important in your family? Can you name three people in English?

screens.title: Family words
screens.body: Study the family words from Welcome B. Say each word aloud and connect it with someone in the family tree.

items.example: My aunt is my mum's sister.

screens.prompt: Notice the relationship words. Some describe women, some men, and some can describe both.

screens.title: Sort the family words
screens.body: Choose the correct category for each word. Based on the family vocabulary table in Workbook, page 5, Exercise 1.

questions.q: Which word belongs in the FEMALE column?
questions.why: Niece means a brother's or sister's daughter.

questions.q: Which word belongs in the MALE column?
questions.why: Nephew means a brother's or sister's son.

questions.q: Which word can describe BOTH male and female family members?
questions.why: Cousin can be a boy or a girl.

questions.q: Which plural family word includes mum and dad?
questions.why: Parents means a mother and a father.

screens.prompt: Can you think of one example for each category?

screens.title: Read a family tree
screens.body: Study the family relationships. Max is the speaker in the family-tree activity in Student's Book, page 6, Exercise 1.
screens.text: Clive and Margaret are Max's grandparents. Paul and Caroline are Max's parents. Mark and Sharon are his aunt and uncle. James is his brother. Harriet is his sister. Bella and Brendan are his cousins.
screens.prompt: Use the family tree to explain how two people are related.

screens.title: Who is who?
screens.body: Practise the relationships from Student's Book, page 6, Exercise 2. Choose the correct word for each relationship.
screens.prompt: Check the generations in the family tree before you answer.

screens.title: Grammar Lab · Plural nouns
screens.body: Student's Book, page 6: regular and irregular plural nouns. Welcome B practises both spelling patterns and irregular forms.
screens.prompt: Look for patterns. Which plural forms add -s, which add -ies, and which change completely?

screens.title: Make it plural
screens.body: Choose the correct plural form. Based on Student's Book, page 6, Exercise 4 and Workbook, page 5, Exercise 2.

questions.why: Woman has an irregular plural: women.
Child has an irregular plural: children.
The plural used here is people.

screens.prompt: Explain one spelling rule in your own words.

screens.title: Grammar Lab · Possessive adjectives
screens.body: Use possessive adjectives to show who something belongs to. The complete set in Grammar Reference W.2 is: my, your, his, her, its, our, their.
screens.prompt: Remember: a possessive adjective comes before a noun.

screens.title: Whose family is it?
screens.body: Choose the correct possessive adjective. Based on Student's Book, page 7, Exercise 7 and Workbook, page 5, Exercises 3–4.

questions.q: This is a photo of ___ family. (I)
This is ___ cat. (me and my brother)

screens.prompt: Find the person or thing in brackets. Which pronoun does it match?

screens.title: Grammar Lab · This, that, these, those
screens.body: Use this and these for people or things near you (here). Use that and those for people or things farther away (there). This/that go with singular nouns; these/those go with plural nouns.
screens.prompt: First decide: is it near or far? Then decide: singular or plural.

screens.title: Here or there? One or more?
screens.body: Choose the demonstrative and the correct form of be. Based on Student's Book, page 7, and Workbook, page 5, Exercise 5.

questions.q: One photo near you: ___ is my photo.
Two dogs near you: ___ are my dogs.
One house farther away: ___ is my house.
Several cousins near you: ___ are my cousins.
One phone near you: ___ is my new phone.
Several brothers farther away: ___ are my brothers.

screens.prompt: Say the full sentence aloud after choosing.

screens.title: Reading · A family photo
screens.body: Read the short texts from the Student's Book, page 7, Exercise 5. Identify the family members and notice the possessive adjectives.
screens.text: James and Max are at a festival. Their friend Vicky is with them. She likes the band. James likes the festival. Harriet is with the family dog after a long walk. The family members are happy, excited, tired or hungry.
screens.prompt: Can you find three possessive adjectives in the text?

screens.title: Speaking task · Guess the relative
screens.body: Based on Student's Book, page 6, Exercise 3 and page 7, Exercise 10.
screens.scenario: Work with a partner. Write five sentences about people in your family tree. Your partner guesses the person. Then draw a simple family tree and ask questions about it.
prompts: Sharon's my mum. Who is she?
No, I'm not. Are you Brendan?
Who is Ben? He's her brother.
screens.prompt: Use family words, possessive adjectives and the verb be.

screens.title: Project Workshop · My Family Tree
screens.body: Add a family tree to your My World Profile. You can use real relatives, or invent a family if you prefer not to share personal information.

fields.label: Caption for your family tree
fields.placeholder: This is my family. These are ...

screens.prompt: Your project now has an identity card and a family tree. Keep your sentences simple and accurate.

visual.alt: Family portrait for a family tree

screens.title: Reflection · My family, my words
screens.body: Check what you can do now. This self-assessment contributes to your learning record.
questions: I can name close and extended family members.
I can explain simple family relationships.
I can make regular and irregular plural nouns.
I can use this, that, these and those.
screens.prompt: Which part would you like to practise again?

screens.title: Mission complete!
screens.body: You have completed the current learning route. Your My World Profile now includes your identity and family tree.
